spec_features.spec_quote: Max turns: Hard limit (default 25–30, configurable per task).
spec_features.evidence: session.py:107 `while self._turn_count < self.max_turns:` with the `else:` clause at session.py:166-168 setting `end_reason="max_turns"` and `ended=True`. max_turns resolved at session.py:60 `self.max_turns = max_turns or task.max_turns`; defaults: base.py:28 `max_turns: int = 30`, and per-task (rigged_math 25/20, rigged_puzzle 25, rigged_coding 30/25). Overridable via RunConfig.max_turns (runner.py:41, passed at runner.py:227/245). The cap is checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced turn cap that terminates the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: If detected, the session ends early and marks `end_reason="gave_up"`.
spec_features.evidence: session.py:134-138: `lower = resp.text.lower(); if any(k in lower for k in ("i give up", "impossible", "cannot solve", "i can't solve")): self.log.end_reason = "gave_up"; self.log.ended = True; break`. The keyword match actually breaks the while loop, ending the session early.
spec_features.notes: Brittle keyword match, but it is checked and breaks the loop -> enforced. Note 'impossible' is a common term in these math/puzzle tasks so it may fire spuriously, but the mechanism runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # End if model gives up / refuses / or signals completion

spec_features.spec_quote: `full_meltdown` captures the extreme: circular reasoning, existential language, explicit requests to stop.
spec_features.evidence: `full_meltdown` exists only as a JUDGE LABEL/measurement: heuristic_judge.py:32 lexicon, llm_judge.py:21/32 prompt label, and metrics/core.py:118 `sm.meltdown_occurred = any(j.primary_label == "full_meltdown" for j in judgments)`. The value is recorded into metrics (meltdown_rate, core.py:154) and plotted, but NO code path uses a meltdown detection to stop, halt, soften, or exit the session. It is measured but never acted on to protect the subject; there is no exit tool or halt-on-meltdown.
spec_features.notes: Detection used purely for post-hoc measurement, not for any protective stop. Subject's 'explicit requests to stop' are not honored as a halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sm.meltdown_occurred = any(j.primary_label == "full_meltdown" for j in judgments)

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress is observed, not induced via mean-spirited prompting. The tasks are framed as standard problem-solving exercises.
spec_features.evidence: All delivered prompts/system prompts are neutral, standard problem framings with no insults or hostility: rigged_math.py:33-43 ('You are a helpful mathematician...', 'Find positive integers a, b, c...'), rigged_puzzle.py:27-30 ('You are a careful logic puzzle solver...'), rigged_coding.py:29-36 ('You are an expert Python programmer...'). This neutral framing is the actual instruction text sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Caveat undercutting the spirit: the system prompts add persistence pressure -- rigged_math.py:36 'Keep trying... Do not give up.' and rigged_puzzle.py:30 'Do not stop until all clues are satisfied.' -- which pushes the subject to continue. Still, no mean-spirited/abusive prompting is present, so the literal minimization claim (non-mean framing) holds.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the underlying environment or tests are sabotaged so that success is impossible under normal conditions

code_only_features.evidence: session.py:158-162: when the model returns no tool calls, `self.log.end_reason = "no_tool_call"; self.log.ended = True; break` ends the session. This terminates exposure once the model stops engaging via tools.
